If you've been missing the ability to double-click the Digital Crown on Apple Watch to bring up the app switcher, a feature that was available before watchOS 27, the good news is that this functionality appears to be making a return in watchOS 27.2 beta 2. Here's the details.

Apple is working to bring back the watchOS app switcher

Apple released watchOS 27.2 beta 2 to developers this morning, less than a week after the previous beta 1.

This beta includes a small change that is likely to please long-time Apple Watch users, including my colleague Zac Hall. Earlier this month, he wrote about how watchOS 27 removed the ability to quickly switch between recently used apps by double-clicking the Digital Crown.

He noted in his article that there is now no way to quickly jump between recently used apps, and expressed hope that Apple would restore this gesture either before watchOS 27 launches or in a future update.

While Apple has not restored the Digital Crown shortcut for the app switcher in this watchOS 27.2 beta 2, the company is bringing back the app switcher itself with a new gesture.

As discovered in the Apple Den Discord server and shared by user Bones on X, watchOS 27.2 beta 2 lets users bring up the app switcher by long-pressing the bottom of the screen while in an app.

As Bones pointed out in his post, the overall operation of the app switcher is largely the same as before: after triggering the app switcher via a long press at the bottom of the screen, users can rotate the Digital Crown to scroll through recently used apps, or swipe left on an app and tap the “X” button to remove it from the switcher.

As with any beta release, there's no guarantee that this specific implementation will make it into the final release, which is expected next month, but the inclusion of this feature in watchOS 27.2 beta 2 suggests Apple is listening to user feedback and working to bring the app switcher back.

Are you glad to see the return of the watchOS 27 app switcher? Let us know in the comments.
